**Overview**

This summary outlines your medical history, focusing on a recent shoulder injury and its management. We'll cover your allergies, the details of the injury, the treatments you received, and the results of various examinations. Please read through this at your own pace, and remember that I'm here to help if anything feels unclear or overwhelming.

**Allergies**

You have a known allergy to sesame. Please always inform healthcare providers of this allergy to prevent any adverse reactions.

**Diagnosis & Examination Findings**

You were diagnosed with a fracture of your shoulder (humerus). Diagnostic imaging revealed a displaced fracture with bone fragments, as seen on X-ray and confirmed by CT scan. A range of motion exam indicated significantly limited movement in your shoulder.

**Surgical History**

To address the fracture, you underwent open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of the fractured humerus. This procedure involved surgically realigning the bone fragments and securing them with internal fixation devices.

**Symptoms**

Following the injury and during your recovery, you experienced shoulder pain, swelling, and a continued limitation in your range of motion.

**Treatments**

Your treatment plan included several components to support healing and manage your symptoms. These included immobilization of the shoulder to allow the bone to heal, pain management strategies to keep you comfortable, and physical therapy to gradually restore range of motion and strength.

**Important Note:** This summary is for informational purposes only and should not be considered a substitute for professional medical advice. If you have any concerns or questions, please don't hesitate to discuss them with your doctor or other qualified healthcare provider. Opt for whole wheat crusts when available, load up on veggies (peppers, onions, spinach), and use lean protein like grilled chicken or turkey instead of pepperoni. **Movement Habits:**
